title: Sparsified epochal cursor slicing to shrink long-scroll dashboard latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Long-scroll workflows in the Console (ex: large tenant event timelines, ‘explore’ view with multi-filter pivoting) exhibit heavy P99 tail latency and CPU spikes. The root cause enabled by our analysis is: linear scans over dense time-series segments + repeated rehydration of cursor payloads for offsets > 10k. Current approaches (cursor over raw rows, naive over-reads, and large per-tenant materialized windows) either increase read amplification or blow memory/cpu on the query plane.

Goal: Reduce P95/P99 for long-scroll and deep-pagination queries by minimizing coordinated scanning work and improving cache hit behavior without increasing per-tenant storage costs. Target: P99 end-to-end latency for 50k-row scrolls reduced from ~6s -> <1.8s (3x improvement) and 20-30% CPU reduction on query workers under representative tenant workloads.

Proposed approach (high-level):
1) Epochal cursor slicing: divide large result sets into logical epochs (time/sequence windows) and encode cursors as a compact epoch identifier + intra-epoch offset. This allows fast epoch skipping without deserializing full KV payloads for previous epochs.
2) Sparsified index summaries: maintain a lightweight per-shard sparse summary (multi-level sampling points every N rows, dense near hot boundaries) persisted as an append-only micro-index. This enables O(log epochs) jump-to-approximate-offset followed by small local scan instead of full scans.
3) Read hedging + micro-prefetch: on epoch boundary requests, issue speculative micro-reads to 2x small-range peers with a hedged timeout to mitigate straggler shards. Micro-prefetch results are cached in an LRU-backed in-memory slice cache keyed by (tenant, epoch-id, sample-anchor).
4) Tenant-aware caching and TTLs: hot tenants get adaptive slice cache TTLs based on query velocity and cardinality estimates. Cold tenants continue to use on-disk indexes. Cache admission respects memory budgets with per-tenant caps to avoid noisy-neighbor effects.

Implementation plan:
- Schema: add epoch_id and sample_anchor metadata to existing cursor protobuf (backwards-compatible optional fields).
- Index: implement micro-index writer in the stream emitter path (batch job to backfill existing shards). Store index files with compact deltas and an accompanying bloom hint for quick membership tests.
- Query API: adapt query router to accept epochal cursors and perform jump-to-epoch logic. Introduce hedged-read path in query worker.
- Cache: implement slice-cache service within the query workers (bounded local LRU) with metrics for hit/miss/eviction and memory footprint.
- Telemetry: new tracing spans for epoch-jump, hedged-read, local-cache-hit and cache-evict; add dedicated dashboard in console-2026.03 release for rollout monitoring.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Complexity: introduces micro-index maintenance and new cursor semantics. We keep migration backwards-compatible and add a feature-flag gated rollout.
- Consistency: epochal cursors approximate offsets; strong correctness requires careful semantics around concurrent writes. We will define cursor-as-liveness-snapshot: epochs are cut at commit time; cursors only guarantee approximate ordering, not exact row IDs. This is acceptable for dashboard exploration UX (we avoid strict cursor semantics used in export/ETL paths).
- Storage cost: micro-indexes add ~2-7% storage overhead per shard (depends on sampling density); will measure in staging.

Testing & rollout:
- Unit tests for cursor encoding/decoding and micro-index lookups.
- Synthetic load test within perf-cluster with tenant mixes (S, M, L). Target runs: 50k-scroll scenarios and multi-user concurrency.
- Canary: enable feature flag for 5 internal tenants -> 50 external low-traffic tenants -> broader rollout tied to release console-2026.03. Monitor p99, CPU, cache hit ratio, and latency SLOs.

Success criteria:
- P99 improved to target for representative workloads
- Slice-cache hit ratio > 60% for hot tenants
- No increase in error rate or out-of-memory incidents in canary

Related tickets: ENG-30482, ENG-20763, ENG-21104
